name: write-artifact
content:
{ "SKILL.md": " # Artifact An artifact is a static page you write so the person can see a result on screen instead of reading it in the chat. It is a folder with an `index.html`. There is no artifact tool: you make one by writing files. ## Where it goes An artifact belongs to a domain. Its place is `domains//artifacts//` in lophn's data, and a domain is one of the domains listed in your place information. Write `//index.html` with `file.write`. `` is the absolute `artifacts` folder of that domain, given in the Artifacts section of your place information. Always use that absolute path: a relative `artifacts/...` path lands in the person's project folder, which is wrong. `` is a lowercase slug (`spending`, `weekly-report`). Once an `index.html` exists at that spot, it is an artifact. Tell the person its path in your answer; the path becomes a link that opens it. The same name in two domains is two artifacts. ## Who writes An agent working in a project or app writes the artifacts of the domains it works with. At home an agent writes no files. ## Folder shape ``` /spending/ ├── index.html the entry and the template ├── chart.js any file in the same folder, read by relative path └── data/ ├── 2026-01.json └── 2026-02.json ``` - `index.html` is required. Other files (`chart.js`, `style.css`, images) sit next to it and are loaded by relative path. A relative link to another HTML file in the folder works. - `data/*.json` is the material the template reads. You usually build it by running a command (for example an aggregate from `lophn kind list`) and writing the result into `data/`. ## How the data is held Three ways, chosen by how the template reads `data/`. They are not kinds. - **One-off:** put the data inside `index.html`. - **Swap:** keep the template and rewrite only `data/latest.json`. - **Series:** keep adding files to `data/`, and let the template read `data/_entries.json`. `data/_entries.json` is a virtual file the view makes. Do not write it to disk. It is a JSON array of `{ "name", "size", "modified" }`, sorted by name, files directly in `data/` only (no subfolders). `modified` is an ISO time. ```js const entries = await (await fetch("data/_entries.json")).json(); const months = await Promise.all( entries.map((e) => fetch(`data/${e.name}`).then((r) => r.json())), ); ``` ## Title and description Always write `` and `<meta name="description" content="...">` in `index.html`. The artifact list and the prompt show these two. Without a `<title>` the folder name is used. Keep the title short and the description to one sentence. ## The view is sealed - There is no network. `fetch` reaches only files in the artifact's own folder; any outside server is blocked. - No external library and no CDN. Scripts, styles and fonts are inline or files in the same folder. If you need a chart, draw it with inline SVG, canvas, or a small script you write into the folder. - One file can be at most 4 MiB. - Files outside the folder, other artifacts and the person's documents cannot be read. - The page has no lophn bridge. It cannot run commands or read app data. It shows what is already in the folder. ## Appearance Use lophn's tokens as CSS variables. The page already has them, so it follows the person's theme (light or dark, and their appearance settings) without any setup. Do not hard-code colors as hex; a hard-coded color stays the same in dark mode and looks wrong. | Variable | Use | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `--color-surface-floor` | page background | | `--color-surface-base` | cards and panels | | `--color-surface-subtle` | table stripes, quiet areas | | `--color-border-base` | borders and rules | | `--color-text-primary` | main text | | `--color-text-secondary` | secondary text | | `--color-text-muted` | captions and axis labels | | `--color-link` | links | | `--status-good-text`, `--status-warning-text`, `--status-critical-text` | status text; `-marker` for dots and bars | | `--chart-series-0` to `--chart-series-7` | chart series colors, in order | | `--font-sans`, `--font-mono` | fonts | | `--type-body-size`, `--type-title-size` | text sizes (also `--type-*-line`) | | `--space-*`, `--radius-sm`, `--radius-md` | spacing and corners | Example: ```css body { background: var(--color-surface-floor); color: var(--color-text-primary); font-family: var(--font-sans); } ``` ## Drawing nodes with the kit The kit draws a node diagram. It is the one library the sealed view gives you, and it works in a workflow artifact and in a domain artifact. - Load it with a plain `<script>` (not a module) and a stylesheet: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_lophn/kit.css">` and `<script src="/_lophn/kit.js"></script>`. - Call `LophnKit.renderGraph(element, { nodes, edges })`. Calling it again on the same element updates it. The element must be a block with a width that is not 0 (not hidden, not `display: inline`). - A node is `{ id, label, status?: { label, tone }, note? }`. `tone` must be one of `good`, `warning`, `serious`, `critical`, `neutral`. `note` is a short text. An edge is `{ from, to, label? }`. - If the data breaks a rule, the whole diagram is drawn as unreadable (error), not just the bad part. The rules: every `id` is non-empty and unique; the `from` and `to` of every edge are ids of existing nodes; an edge from a node to itself is not allowed (leave it out); `tone` is one of the five values. A cycle (A to B and back to A) is fine. - What a status value means is yours to decide (for example `running` for the current step and `reported` when a report exists). ## Drawing a domain A domain artifact can draw the domain as nodes. It is optional: before you make one, ask the person with `ask` whether they want a picture. None is a good answer. Do not make one without asking. Two things are worth drawing: - **Kind map:** each kind is a node and each `ref` field is an edge from the kind that has the field to the kind in `to`, with the field name as the edge `label`. A `ref` to its own kind would be an edge from a node to itself: leave it out and, if it matters, say it in the node's `note`. For the number of items, run `lophn kind list` with a count aggregate for each kind and put it in the `note`. - **State flow:** if a kind has an `enum` field that means a state (`status`, `stage`), each value is a node. Run `lophn kind list` with the same aggregate and a group-by on that field, and put the number of items of each value in the `note`. The order between values (the edges) is the domain's meaning: take it from `DOMAIN.md` or from what the person says. If you do not know it, draw the values with no edges. The artifact cannot read `kinds.yaml` or run a command, so you write the diagram data into `data/*.json` yourself (for example `data/map.json` with `nodes` and `edges`) and the page reads it. When the kinds change, change the data too. ```html <!doctype html> <title>Kind map
``` with, for example, `data/map.json`: ```json { "nodes": [ { "id": "receipt", "label": "receipt", "note": "42 items" }, { "id": "vendor", "label": "vendor", "note": "7 items" } ], "edges": [{ "from": "receipt", "to": "vendor", "label": "vendor" }] } ``` ## Changes show at once When you change a file in the folder, a tab that has it open reloads. There are no versions: to keep earlier data, add files to `data/` instead of overwriting. To go back, the person uses rewind. ## When the person sends annotations The person can mark the screen and send notes. They go to the last open session that wrote to that artifact's folder, as a message. If there is none (those sessions are closed or have no record), lophn at the project or app that holds the domain gets them. Open the screenshot with `image.read`. ## What you do not do - Do not make a page that runs commands or reads live app data. A screen like that is an app, which is built in a conversation at that app. " }
